newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. astronomer Shoemaker dies in Australia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. astronomer Shoemaker dies in Australia.

text.p: U.S. astronomer Eugene Shoemaker, who helped discover the giant Shoemaker-Levy 9 comet which slammed into the planet Jupiter in 1994, died in a car crash in outback Australia, police said on Saturday.
Shoemaker's astronomer wife Carolyn was injured in the head-on collision with another car on Friday afternoon, said police sergeant Neville Pulfard from Alice Springs in central Australia.
The accident occurred on a dirt road near the border of the Northern Territory and Western Australia state, about 500 km (300 miles) northwest of Alice Springs.
Police said Shoemaker, 69, and his wife were on a combined holiday and search for meteor impact sites.
Carolyn Shoemaker has been airlifted to Alice Springs hospital and is in a satisfactory condition.
The Shoemakers, along with astronomer David Levy, discovered the comet Shoemaker-Levy 9, which broke up and slammed into Jupiter in 1994. The crash caused an explosion which could be seen from Earth.
Shoemaker was also involved in several U.S. space missions, including the Apollo missions to the moon.
